newsitem.title: USA: Rawlings sees modest Q1 loss, lower revs.
newsitem.headline: Rawlings sees modest Q1 loss, lower revs.

text.p: Rawlings Sporting Goods Co Inc said Wednesday it expects to report a modest net loss for the fiscal first quarter ending November 30 and revenues for the quarter that will be below last year.

Rawlings added that the expected loss for the quarter and the revenue projection are below its internal expectations. A year ago, the company had net income of $890,000 or $0.12 a share on sales of $35.5 million.

The projected decline in net revenues is expected to result from lower sales of baseballs, primarily in the collectible market, and baseball gloves, primarily the result of several large retailers not purchasing significant quantities of baseball gloves in the quarter, Rawlings said. The company
also said basketballs have recently begun to show weakness at retail.
"The baseball collectible market has softened," Carl Shields, chairman, said in a statement.

"The Cal Ripken Jr commemorative baseball contributed significantly to baseball net revenues in the quarter ended November 30, 1995, with no comparable product in 1996. Not only is this business not being replaced but revenues from other commemorative baseballs have declined as well," Shields added.
The trend toward later shipments to retainers continues, and a major warehouse club customer is exiting the baseball category, the chairman said.

"These factors are expected to result in significantly lower net revenues of baseball gloves in the quarter," Shields said. "While the results for the first quarter are disappointing, many large retailers are expecting strong sell-through this spring. If strong spring sell-through occurs, the company is well positioned to take advantage of the situation."
